description:
The campaign provenance's cpu_model field records the producer's OS-and-architecture token rather than the host CPU identity, so committed receipts do not name the hardware that produced machine-dependent work counters and timings.

## Background

Receipts record provenance.runtime.cpu_model as a platform token such as linux-x86_64. The claims-trace-to-artifacts invariant expects committed evidence to record hardware identity; a platform token cannot distinguish hosts with different microarchitectures. The provenance note of the affected campaign states the limitation and records the host in prose, which is a workaround rather than tool-observed fact.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The provenance runtime section records the runtime-observed CPU model string (and core/thread counts) of the producing host.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test asserts the recorded cpu_model is the observed processor identity, not an OS or architecture token.
- [hard] REQ-03: Existing committed receipts remain readable and their platform-token fields are documented as the prior format.
title: campaign provenance cpu_model records a platform token, not the CPU model
